_comment: How sources are read, separately from which model reasons over what is read.
A skill declares WHAT it needs; this declares HOW, so a blocked path is a
backend swap rather than a skill rewrite.
Two runtimes exist on this system and they are NOT interchangeable. Patrick OS
once reported that autonomous Reddit research was impossible; that was measured
against the Mac install and stated as a fact about the world. Capability is now
PROBED from the runtime that will do the work -- `patrick retrieval probe`.
backend_order is a fallthrough chain, not a preference list. An empty result
from one backend is not the same finding as 'there is nothing there', and
the chain exists so the two are never confused.

hermes-beastmaster._note: Hermes v0.20.4. toolsets hermes-cli/web/search/browser; web.search_backend=tavily, web.extract_backend=browser; default gpt-5.6-sol via openai-codex, whose credential pool holds 2 entries. VERIFIED 2026-09-04: a live search of r/passive_income returned real Reddit permalinks with content. This is the retrieval runtime.

hermes-mac._note: Hermes v0.13.0. No web backend configured, browser disabled, credential pool holds only copilot and nous. CANNOT do web research, and its limits must never be generalized to Beastmaster -- doing exactly that produced the false claim that Reddit retrieval required OAuth credentials.

hermes-web.how: Search first via Hermes' web/search toolsets, then extract with the browser, then fall back to a public archive where direct extraction is blocked. Original Reddit permalinks are preserved as the citation throughout.
hermes-web.verified: 2026-09-04 against r/passive_income: real permalinks and real content returned.
hermes-web.note: Requires a runtime with web+search toolsets and a search backend. hermes-beastmaster has them; hermes-mac does not. Non-deterministic in practice; reddit-archive is the fallthrough when it yields nothing.

reddit-api.how: Reddit's official API with a registered script app.
reddit-api.note: An OPTIONAL structured fallback, not a prerequisite. Useful for exhaustive windowed pulls where search recall is the limit. Nothing here implements it.

manual-export.how: A human pastes or exports the threads into the skill's input.
manual-export.note: Final fallback. Slow, and it always works.

direct-fetch.how: Raw HTTP GET against reddit.com while logged out.
direct-fetch.blocked_reason: Reddit serves a 'Prove your humanity' anti-bot challenge. Verified 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-04.
direct-fetch.note: Recorded so nobody tries it again and draws the wrong conclusion. A blocked direct fetch does NOT mean Reddit research is unavailable -- search-first retrieval works. Workers are explicitly told not to begin here.

reddit-archive.how: Query the Arctic Shift public Reddit archive over HTTP, directly from Python. Returns author, permalink, date and verbatim body as structured data.
reddit-archive.verified: 2026-09-04: 34 items from r/passive_income in a 90-day window.
reddit-archive.note: Deterministic where hermes-web is not: the same hermes-web request returned 12 items on one run and 0 on the next, because an agent was rediscovering the archive each time and its queries timed out. Nothing here is a model, so nothing here can invent a permalink. This is the archive rung of the search-first ladder, reached because direct Reddit extraction is always blocked.
